questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I chose Oslo because of the courses they had available for biology students. I also liked that the culture and country was very similar to my home country.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: At the University of Oslo you barely have classes which I found very weird. So most of the time I was just studying on my own.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Was easy I was guided through everything in emails.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I applied through SiO. There are many student towns in Olso so it was very easy to find a place off campus. However you are not guaranteed an apartment in the student houses you apply for. They might just put you somewhere available.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
Make sure there are good transportation options. In the nights there are only night busses which can be a pain as they are always overfilled. 
Living off campus is nice especially when living near the lakes and forests.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You find courses you like and add them in the terminal. The registration is super late and you are not guaranteed spots so you have the opportunity to choose more courses than needed.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I did not use any.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I registered for 4 classes and got into all four. However I only needed 3 courses so I dropped one of them.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Add many courses
Do not get your hopes too high on certain courses
If you do not get into a courses, put yourself on the waitlist, you might get lucky. A friend of mine was number 3 on the waitlist and still got into the course she wanted.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It was as you should expect on a bachelor level.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
At UiO there are many lectures and in some courses they only have lectures which is super boring. UiO had a lot of guest speakers which we do not at UCPH.
At UCPH we usually have smaller classes within a course where we answer questions and discuss the topic.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Marine Biology
Norwegian life and society 
Norwegian beginner 60 hour course

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Norwegian for beginners. The Norwegian for beginners is not only great for learning the language but also getting to know other exchange students.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Everything in the supermarket is crazy expensive.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Clothes is fairly cheap, gym membership is cheap, rent is cheap.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Anything imaginable. They had a club for everything.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I climbed and skateboarded while being there which is a great way to meet new people.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Travel around Norway. I went to Bergen, Trondheim, Lillehammer, Røros and sightseeing in Oslo. There is plenty to do. You can go by train many places and the view is amazing.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy it is basically the same as in Denmark.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Don't lol. The locals are hard to reach and they prefer being with other Norwegians. I would recommend climbing or going to the bar if you want to find Norwegians but still in those places they are not particularly welcoming.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Going hiking and being outside every time you can.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1 apply for student housing where you share a kitchen with others (I lived in Sogn even though I didnt apply for Sogn and it was great)
2 do not expect to be friends with Norwegians
3 save up money, the supermarkets are expensive

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I would have liked to know that even though you do not apply for certain student houses they might still place you there. And you cannot say no to the spot given.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The nature and the people I meet on this journey

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer:
Loneliness, even though you have friends and people in your kitchen, it is very easy to feel alone. Your family is not here and your best friends are not here.
I had great friends that I saw several times during the week, I went on trips with people and there was always someone to talk to in my kitchen. But still you lay at night feeling the loneliness some days.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
